title: Ellsworth inner zone alert: saucer beams light at missile
place_text: Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota

and as we turned left there sat this object on top of November 5 that was about 10 ft in the air directly on top of that blast door that was the size of a Walmart building
tellings.difference: Dates it to 1977 rather than the 1960s, names site November-5 and says the object was the size of a Walmart, with no reddish beam mentioned.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe a saucer hovering over a missile site at Ellsworth that the security team was sent to check. This telling gives Mario Woods' view of the object over November-5.

tellings.link_reason: Hastings sums up the same Mario Woods case at Ellsworth: after the encounter, Woods, his partner and the truck ended up five miles away at a reservoir.

as_told.title: Mario Woods sees a light to the east
as_told.place_text: Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota

plain: Mario Woods, a former security guard at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, says that one night he and his partner, Michael Johnson, found an object "the size of a Walmart building" hovering about ten feet over the blast door of a nuclear missile site called November 5. Woods tells it firsthand: he says he looked at his watch at 12:15 and next found it was after 6 a.m., with the two men and their truck moved miles away to a reservoir, the mud around the truck strangely warm on a freezing night, and his partner unresponsive. The researcher Robert Hastings and Michels also retell it, Michels once adding a report of a flying saucer sending "a beam of reddish light" down at the missile, though the tellers disagree on whether it happened in the 1960s or in 1977 or 1978, and on whether the men were moved five, eight and a half, or nine miles.
